A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same active prompt learning framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original active learning experiments, prompt-learning comparisons, base-to-novel generalization results and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports revised experiments and additional ImageNet, ISIC, KaoKore, backbone and acquisition-method evaluations, including Appendix D.

M1.justification: Equation 7 changes class-guided features from averaging image and weighted text embeddings to concatenating them. Section 4.3 also introduces combined unified and class-wise prompts, averaging their cosine scores in new Equation 14; v1 used unified prompts. These alter the representation and prediction procedure, while the clustering and selective-querying framework remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet classification and the medical ISIC and illustrated-image KaoKore domains. Its main benchmark suite changes from nine datasets to seven, incorporating EuroSAT, which v1 already tested in a failure analysis. Food101, SUN397 and UCF101 remain represented in the retained nine-dataset base-to-novel results.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds substantive initial-selection comparisons involving TypiClust, ProbCover, its K-means variant and DropQuery, with image-only and class-guided features. This expands comparison beyond the earlier random-initialization controls. The main Random, Entropy, CoreSet, BADGE and PCB comparator set and the three model-centric prompt-learning baselines remain.

E3.justification: The main comparison changes from unified CoOp prompts without LLM descriptions to baseline training with class-wise prompts and LLM descriptions. v2 adds unified/class-wise/combined prompt controls, a four-shot StanfordCars confidence diagnostic, and DTD evaluations using CLIP ViT-L/14-336 and EVA01-CLIP-g-14-plus. The eight-round schedule and per-round budget equal to the class count remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test selective querying across acquisition types, prompt-dependent confidence and overfitting, domain/backbone robustness, and class-guided features within additional acquisition methods. v1's EuroSAT incorrect-guidance analysis and Euclidean-versus-cosine clustering comparison disappear. The increasing-K ablation is retained as v2 Table 6, and the earlier prompt-type comparison is substantially expanded.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averages over three trials and standard-deviation shading. Point estimates and mean-plus-spread tables remain the reporting practices; v2 introduces no new seed counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Main curves and Tables 1–2 are revised. The reported initial advantage changes from v1's 2.7% to v2's 19.5 percentage points, and budget savings from 26% to 17.6%, under different method, prompt and dataset settings. These are not same-setting gains. New ImageNet and Appendix D results appear, while the two-shot transfer table disappears. Figure 4's class-guided ARIs change from 57.33/39.68% to 56.57/37.64%.

T1.justification: The mathematical feature definition changes in Equation 7, and Equation 14 introduces the combined-prompt similarity definition. The threshold, loss and GradFAM formulations otherwise remain substantially intact; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions—class-guided clustering, cluster-balanced acquisition and budget-saving selective querying—remain. The abstract changes its main experimental scope from nine to seven datasets, while the conclusion adds an explicit claim of applicability to ImageNet-scale settings and scalable VLM adaptation.

C2.justification: v2 explains selective-querying benefits through diversity-based selection and reduced confidence overfitting with unified prompts. It interprets new domain/backbone results as broader applicability evidence. The concrete EuroSAT incorrect-guidance limitation is removed, while new limitations address dependence on strong pretrained models, classification-only validation and untested real human-in-the-loop deployment.

D1.justification: v2 explains duplicating image features to match GradFAM dimensions and documents the confidence diagnostic's four-shot subset, per-class averaging and 50-bin histograms. Exact additional backbone identifiers are supplied. The 16-vector initialization, 200 epochs and SGD schedule already appeared in v1 Appendix B and are moved into Section 5.1.

R1.justification: The related-work framing remains largely unchanged. v2 adds references supporting ImageNet-scale active learning, LLM descriptions, additional prompt designs, backbones and datasets, while removing several dataset references. Appendix D explicitly acknowledges that its initial selection operates like DropQuery, differing through class-guided features.

P1.justification: The introduction, algorithm wording and conclusion are revised, implementation details move into the main setup, and supplementary sections are regrouped. The main section sequence and much of the related-work, preliminary and methodological prose remain, so the language and structural revision is limited relative to the scientific additions.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two columns to a single-column TMLR layout. The framework diagram is updated, benchmark panels and table columns are reorganized, and new confidence, acquisition and ImageNet displays appear. v1's two supplementary GradFAM figures are merged into v2 Figure 10, alongside other figure/table additions and removals.

improvement.justification: Prompt-controlled comparisons and confidence analyses better support the explanation of selective querying, while stronger initial-selection comparators and new domain, scale and backbone tests improve the evidence for applicability. However, retained results are not fully reconciled with the revised method: v2 Figure 4 reports Waterbirds ARIs of 56.57/37.64%, whereas Appendix Figure 14 retains 57.33/39.68% without explaining the difference. The additional evidence supports a net improvement, but these consistency gaps limit its extent.
